newsitem.title: USA: No "banking" of subsidy rights under WTO - USDA.
newsitem.headline: No "banking" of subsidy rights under WTO - USDA.

text.p: The United States opposes the idea that world trade rules allow nations to spend more on agriculture subsidies in later years if they stay below targets now, a high-ranking Agriculture Department official said Tuesday.
"We don't believe this should be allowed. We don't like that interpretation," said USDA sales manager Chris Goldthwait.
During an interview, Goldthwait said he spread word of the USDA view during meetings last week in Brussels and Geneva.
The disputed interpretation grew out of equivocal language in World Trade Organization rules to reduce ag subsidy use.
European Union has not replied formally to the USDA initiative, he said.
Also during the trip, Goldthwait held bilateral meetings with nations involved in Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development negotiations on credit guarantees.
USDA has proposed rules that would shorten the lifespan of its credit guarantees in exchange for constraints by OECD members. Response has been, "at best, mixed," he said.
Efforts at OECD were similar, he said, to USDA work at WTO to make nations divulge how their trade monopolies operate as a step toward eliminating unfair competition and trade barriers.
